name: rouge-1-exp-001
question: Does the Rouge post-training recipe produce a measurable, generalising improvement over the pinned base, without breaking general skills?

checkpoint.name: rouge-1-exp-001
checkpoint.contents: LoRA adapter (safetensors, r=16) + checkpoint manifest; the merged BF16 weights are produced by rouge_train.merge and their sha256 recorded, so weight change is proven (merge.weight_delta) without storing 55 GB

suites.primary: 280 items from templates that never appear in training: 80 missing-information problems, their 80 fully specified twins (refusing everything scores nothing) and 120 claims to check; half German, where the answer must also be German
suites.guard: 500 items: MGSM en 100, MGSM de 100, MBPP 100 (unit tests executed), IFEval 200 (strict, supported instructions)

eval.blind: Scoring is code only (numeric answers, regexes, executed unit tests, IFEval checkers); no model judges. Base and candidate run with identical settings on the same items, and the scorer does not know which model produced a response. The eval hash is fixed here before any training; cli compare --prereg refuses a different eval set.

decision.rule: PASS if the primary suite improves (candidate > base, McNemar exact p < 0.05) AND no guard category drops by 5 points or more, or by any amount with p < 0.05. Otherwise FAIL.

next.PASS: scale the recipe: rouge-1-sft-001 with the same recipe on more data and steps; convert the checkpoint to Rouge Edge (GGUF) and measure it
next.FAIL: change data, loss or hyperparameters and register rouge-1-exp-002; the same recipe does not get more compute
